order

Move a column to the end

Stata 

order id, last

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::relocate(data, id, .after=dplyr::last_col())

R dplyr

Move selected columns to the front

Stata

R dplyr

putmata

Copy numeric columns into an R matrix

Stata 

putmata X=(x y)

R base 

X <- as.matrix(data[c('x','y')])

R matrix workflow replaces the separate Mata workspace; X is a fixed matrix name.

Stata reference · R reference

Copy complete numeric rows into a matrix

Stata 

putmata X=(x y), omitmissing

R base 

X <- as.matrix(data[stats::complete.cases(data[c('x','y')]),c('x','y')])

R matrix workflow replaces Mata; rows are removed jointly over the selected columns.

Stata reference · R reference

recode

Recode selected values with Stata rules

Stata 

recode x (1 = 10) (2 = 20), generate(z)

R tidystata 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, z = tidystata::stata_recode(x, 1 ~ 10, 2 ~ 20))

Unmatched values, including missing values, are kept. Rules are compared with the original values, so stata_recode(x, 1 ~ 2, 2 ~ 1) swaps codes. NA ~ 0 recodes missing values, like (missing = 0).

Stata reference · R reference

Recode ranges of values with Stata rules

Stata 

recode x (1/2 = 0) (3/6 = 1) (else = .), generate(binary)

R tidystata 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, binary = tidystata::stata_recode(x, 1:2 ~ 0, 3:6 ~ 1, .default = NA))

In stata_recode() (alias recode()), 1:2 is the closed range 1 <= x <= 2, including decimals, like 1/2 in Stata. The first matching rule wins. .default = NA plays the role of else = .; without it, unmatched values are kept, as in Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

Collapse closed numeric ranges to two groups

Stata 

recode x (1/2=0) (3/6=1), generate(binary)

R tidystata 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, binary = tidystata::stata_recode(x, 1:2 ~ 0, 3:6 ~ 1))

Rules include both endpoints and decimal values; unmatched values stay unchanged.

Stata reference · R reference

Recode selected values and retain all others

Stata 

recode x (1=10) (2=20), generate(z)

R tidystata 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, z = tidystata::stata_recode(x, 1 ~ 10, 2 ~ 20))

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Recode values and label the new codes

Stata 

recode x (min/2 = 0 "Low") (3/max = 1 "High"), generate(level)

R tidystata 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, level = tidystata::stata_recode(x, Low = min:2 ~ 0, High = 3:max ~ 1))

Differs from Stata Named rules give the new codes value labels, and the result is a haven_labelled vector. Old value labels are dropped; the variable label is kept. Stata attaches a new value label set named after the variable.

reshape

Reshape multiple parallel measurement stubs

Stata 

reshape long x y, i(id) j(wave)

R tidyr 

data <- tidyr::pivot_longer(data,cols=c(x1,x2,y1,y2),names_to=c('.value','wave'),names_pattern='([xy])([12])',names_transform=list(wave=as.integer))

Fixed two-stub example; all name patterns and source names must be changed together.

Stata reference · R reference

Convert a wide measurement stub to long rows

Stata 

reshape long x, i(id) j(wave)

R tidyr 

data <- tidyr::pivot_longer(data,cols=c(x1,x2),names_to='wave',names_prefix='x',names_transform=list(wave=as.integer),values_to='x')

Fixed x1/x2 stub example; source names, stub and output names must be changed together.

Stata reference · R reference

Convert unique long measurements to wide columns

Stata 

reshape wide x, i(id) j(wave)

R tidyr 

data <- tidyr::pivot_wider(data,id_cols=id,names_from=wave,values_from=x,names_prefix='x')

Differs from Stata Requires unique id-wave pairs; duplicates must be resolved explicitly rather than silently aggregated.

separate

Create group-specific copies of a numeric column

Stata 

separate x, by(g)

R base 

for (k in sort(unique(data$g))) data[[paste0('x',k)]] <- ifelse(data$g==k,data$x,NA_real_)

Stata reference · R reference

Separate a column by a binary expression

Stata 

separate y, by(g == 1) generate(z)

R base 

data$z0 <- ifelse(data$g!=1,data$y,NA_real_); data$z1 <- ifelse(data$g==1,data$y,NA_real_)

The generated stub z is fixed here; z0 and z1 are the false and true branches.

Stata reference · R reference

xi

Create indicator variables omitting the lowest category

Stata 

xi i.g

R tidystata 

data <- dplyr::select(tidystata::as_dummy(data, g, .names = "index"), -tidyselect::any_of("g_1"))

Differs from Stata Keeps the original columns and omits the first observed category. Numeric categories are ordered by value; R factors follow their level order, which must match Stata's omitted category. Stata names indicators by category code; R numbers observed categories with .names="index". Use factor(g) in models; xi: interactions are not reproduced.
